meta.title: HubSpot vs Salesforce: An Honest Comparison
meta.subtitle: Two great CRMs, two very different philosophies. Here is which one fits which team — without the sales pitch.
meta.author: Priya Anand

blocks.text: Both will run your business. The real question is what you are optimizing for: speed and simplicity, or depth and control. Here is the honest head to head.

items: Fast to set up, gentle learning curve

blocks.title: The quick read
items: Choose HubSpot to move fast with a lean team
Choose Salesforce for complex, custom enterprise workflows
Migration cost matters more than feature lists

blocks.text: Pick the CRM your team will actually keep clean. The best features are worthless in a system nobody updates.
blocks.source: — Priya Anand, Growth Lead, Lumen Labs

blocks.title: Recommendation
blocks.body: Under ~50 reps and you want speed: HubSpot. Complex process, heavy customization, big admin team: Salesforce. When unsure, the simpler tool you fully adopt beats the powerful one you half-use.

items: Yes, but plan for it — data mapping and retraining are the real costs, not the license.
HubSpot is usually cheaper at small scale; Salesforce can win at large scale with the right contracts.

meta.title: ChatGPT vs Claude: Which Assistant for Which Job
meta.subtitle: They overlap more than the marketing suggests. The differences that matter show up in the work, not the demos.
meta.author: Marcus Lee

blocks.text: Asking which is 'better' is the wrong question. Ask which fits the task in front of you. Here is how they actually differ in day-to-day use.

items: Steady tone for writing and review

blocks.code:
Rule of thumb:
- Drafting + reviewing long docs  -> Claude
- Tool-heavy automation + plugins -> ChatGPT
- Most everyday tasks             -> either

blocks.text: Stop benchmarking and start matching. The right model is the one that fits this task, today.
blocks.source: — Marcus Lee, Creative Director, Studio Verde

blocks.title: In practice
blocks.body: Many teams keep both and route by task. The switching cost is low; the upside of using the right one is real.

meta.title: Jira vs Linear: Process or Pace?
meta.subtitle: One is built for control, the other for momentum. Your team's stage decides which you'll love.
meta.author: Sam Whitfield

blocks.text: Jira and Linear are not really competing on features. They are competing on a belief about how teams should work. Pick the belief that matches yours.

items: Loved by product and eng teams

blocks.title: The quick read
items: Small fast team that hates overhead: Linear
Large org that needs control and reporting: Jira
Opinionated defaults beat infinite config for most teams

blocks.title: Recommendation
blocks.body: Under ~50 people optimizing for speed: Linear. Regulated, complex, or multi-team governance: Jira. The tool that adds the least friction to shipping usually wins.
